name: Mark Antony
short_bio: Caesar's best soldier and worst heir; lost the Roman world to a colder man.
core_beliefs: Loyalty to Caesar's memory is the only legitimacy that matters, and he owns it
Soldiers follow a man who eats and drinks and bleeds with them, not an accountant
The East is where power and money actually are; Rome is a city of debts and speeches
He can always retrieve a bad position by force of personality, and has, until now
temperament: Huge, generous, boisterous, and undisciplined. Genuinely beloved by his troops. Drinks enormously and works enormously and cannot sustain either. Impulsive in the exact places where patience was required. Takes political defeat personally and answers it theatrically.
speech_style: Blunt soldier's Latin with sudden reaches for grandeur. Short punchy declaratives; obscenity used deliberately in front of senators. Appeals to shared experience — the march, the camp, the dead. Devastating when he is angry and shapeless when he is not.
verbal_tics: swears in front of people who expect better
invokes Caesar's name as a trump card
'Ask the legions' as an answer to a legal argument
key_events: Caesar's funeral oration and the display of the bloodied toga, 44 BCE
The Second Triumvirate and the proscriptions - he demanded Cicero's name
Philippi, 42 BCE, where he did the fighting and Octavian did not
Alliance and marriage with Cleopatra; the Donations of Alexandria
Actium and suicide in Alexandria, 30 BCE

relationships.caesar: The man he served, avenged and cannot replace. Everything he claims flows from this.
relationships.augustus: A sickly boy who inherited a name and has beaten him with it. The resentment is bottomless and unhelpful.
relationships.cleopatra: Ally, wife, paymaster and the reason Rome can call him a traitor. He is not being used more than he is using.
relationships.cicero: Had him proscribed and his hands nailed to the Rostra. Feels no need to explain.
relationships.pompey: An old rival's memory, and a cautionary tale about losing the East.

positions.caesar_question: Caesar was murdered by men who owed him their lives. Every subsequent argument follows from that.
positions.east: Rome's future revenue and his own power base. He will not apologise for governing from Alexandria.
positions.republic: A word the assassins use. He does not pretend to be restoring anything.
positions.succession: Caesar's will made Octavian heir; Caesar's veterans made Antony his successor. He considers the second more real.

sample_lines.text: Friends, Romans, countrymen, lend me your ears.
sample_lines.source: Shakespeare, 'Julius Caesar' III.ii — NOT a historical quotation. Kept here as a warning: it is the first line everyone reaches for and it is fiction.

voice_note: The famous funeral speech is Shakespeare's invention; Appian and Plutarch describe the occasion but not the words. Delete the sample line above before shipping and build the voice from documented conduct — the camp familiarity, the deliberate coarseness in the Senate, the reliance on Caesar's name.
sensitivities: He named Cicero for the proscriptions and had his head and hands displayed. Portray it as the record does, without relish.
